Gear rental in Islamabad: Ascender Outdoors — trekking gear sales and rental (tents, sleeping bags, stoves, crampons, ice axes), F-11/1, Ali Market, Islamabad, +92 333 9980903, info@ascender.pk. Worth stocking up here before heading north rather than counting on finding gear in-valley.

you're not blamed for pre-existing damage at return.", "metadata": {"page_end": 16, "page_start": 14, "source": "pakistan-north-tours-final.pdf"}}, {"id": "p028-030-6c22e017412e", "text": "Shimshal Pass & Minglik Sar

Start point: Shimshal Valley — reached by a jeep road (the famous Shimshal jeep track) branching off the KKH near Passu, running through Attabad Lake, Gulmit, and Hussaini. This road can be covered by jeep in a day from Hunza — rough enough that most operators use jeeps rather than bikes for it, though it's technically driveable on a light bike in good weather.

What it is: Shimshal Valley (3,000m) is the highest permanent settlement in Hunza, home to about 2,240 households, and the historic gateway used by Hunza raiders on China-India trade routes. Route: Shimshal Village → Korband → Gharsar → Peryan Sar → Shujerab → Shimshal Pass (4,735m) → onward to the Shimshal Lakes and Minglik Sar base camp.

whether contacts, emergency numbers, tour operators, and a cultural calendar were in here. Currency conversions throughout this document use roughly PKR 278 = US$1 (July 2026 rate) — this moves day to day, so treat converted figures as approximate.

Altitude sickness (AMS) — a genuine gap in

this document until now

This list has dozens of treks above 4,000m and several above 5,000m (K2 Base Camp, Gondogoro La, Chilinji Pass, Shimshal Pass, Lohigal An, Zani Pass, Rush Lake), and none of those entries mentioned altitude sickness. That's worth fixing centrally rather than in every single entry.

Symptoms of AMS: headache (the key early sign — a headache above ~3,300m/11,000ft is not "normal," it's a warning), nausea, loss of appetite, dizziness, fatigue, and insomnia.

The rule that matters most: do not continue ascending — especially to a higher sleeping altitude — if symptoms persist. Most of the "moderate/difficult" grading you'll see across this document already builds in acclimatization days for exactly this reason — don't skip them to save time.

When it gets serious: confusion, staggering, or loss of coordination signals HACE (high altitude cerebral edema); breathlessness at rest, persistent

cough, or frothy sputum signals HAPE (high altitude pulmonary edema) — both are life- threatening and can progress to death within about 12 hours. The only real treatment is immediate descent, with medication and oxygen if available.

Diamox (acetazolamide): the standard preventive medication, typically started 1-2 days before a high-altitude ascent — this is a prescription drug, so this isn't medical advice, just a flag that it exists and is widely used by trekkers on exactly this kind of terrain; talk to a doctor before your K2/GGLA or Snow Lake-tier trips specifically, given how high and sustained those are.", "metadata": {"source": "pakistan-north-tours-final.pdf", "page_start": 1, "page_end": 3}}, {"id": "p024-026-a464334daa72", "text": "Karambar Lake Trek

What it is: A high-altitude glacial lake at 4,272m in Ishkoman Valley, Ghizer District — Pakistan's 2nd highest lake, sitting near the Afghan border. Days: 5-day minimum itinerary is typical: Sor Laspur → Lashkargaz (15km) → Karambar Lake via the pass (18km) → rest day → return (18km + 15km). Difficulty: Challenging to extremely challenging — needs solid fitness, prior high-altitude experience, and mental readiness for genuine wilderness with limited acclimatization stops.

Permits: No formal permit currently required for Pakistani citizens from either the Chitral or Gilgit- Baltistan side (this has changed before and could again — worth a local check before you go).

toughest high-altitude passes in the north — a serious add-on for a future, more technical trip.", "metadata": {"page_end": 26, "page_start": 24, "source": "pakistan-north-tours-final.pdf"}}, {"id": "p040-042-e594be504c6e", "text": "K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La (GGLA)

Route: Skardu → jeep to Askole (last village, ~7 hours), then on foot: Jhola → Paiju (rest day) →

Khoburtse → Urdukas → Goro II → Concordia → K2 Base Camp, then either return the same way or cross Gondogoro La (5,585m) down into Hushe Valley.

Distance/days: About 160km total, 12–14 days of trekking plus 4+ days of transport — most full packages run 18–22 days Islamabad to Islamabad.

Elevation: K2 Base Camp itself sits around 5,000m; Gondogoro La is the high point at 5,585m.

Gear/guide: A guide, porter, and CKNP permit are mandatory; crossing Gondogoro La needs crampons, a climbing harness, and a carabiner, with fixed ropes available July–August for a fee (~PKR 28,000 for up to 2 people).

Cost: Getting the letter-of-invitation visa support plus CKNP fee runs about $900 (roughly PKR 250,000), guide+porter+their food roughly separate, and jeep transport in/out about $1,100 (roughly PKR 306,000) — this is genuinely one of the most expensive treks on your whole list, before even counting the guided-package markup.

This is the big one. If you only do one "expedition- grade" trek off this entire 100+ place list, this is the one most people mean when they say it.

Shigar Valley

Shigar town: About 45km / 40–50 min drive from Skardu, on the way to Askole. Home to the 17th-

century Shigar Fort — now a Serena heritage hotel — and the 14th-century Amburiq Mosque.

Arandu Valley & Chogo Lungma Glacier ice caves: About 4 hours by jeep further up-valley from Skardu, in upper Shigar District. Corridor

Getting there

This is the corridor you already pass through on the way to every other region — Kohistan sits between Besham and Chilas on the KKH, and Gilgit sits right where the Hunza road, Skardu road, Naltar turnoff, and Astore turnoff all meet. Kohistan — Palas Valley (Morro Meadows & Takhto Lake)

Route: Islamabad → Besham (4-5 hours) → Dobair Bazaar (~15km further) → Pattan (~25km further,

on the KKH) → cross the Indus bridge at Pattan → jeep track into Palas Valley. Kolai-Palas is its own district now, split from the rest of Kohistan, divided into accessible Lower Palas and the harder-to- reach Upper Palas.

Symptoms of AMS: headache (the key early sign — a headache above ~3,300m/11,000ft is not "normal," it's a warning), nausea, loss of appetite, dizziness, fatigue, and insomnia.

The rule that matters most: do not continue ascending — especially to a higher sleeping altitude — if symptoms persist. Most of the "moderate/difficult" grading you'll see across this document already builds in acclimatization days for exactly this reason — don't skip them to save time.

Getting there from Islamabad/Rawalpindi

whether contacts, emergency numbers, tour operators, and a cultural calendar were in here. Currency conversions throughout this document use roughly PKR 278 = US$1 (July 2026 rate) — this moves day to day, so treat converted figures as approximate.

Altitude sickness (AMS) — a genuine gap in

this document until now

This list has dozens of treks above 4,000m and several above 5,000m (K2 Base Camp, Gondogoro La, Chilinji Pass, Shimshal Pass, Lohigal An, Zani Pass, Rush Lake), and none of those entries mentioned altitude sickness. That's worth fixing centrally rather than in every single entry.

Symptoms of AMS: headache (the key early sign — a headache above ~3,300m/11,000ft is not "normal," it's a warning), nausea, loss of appetite, dizziness, fatigue, and insomnia.

The rule that matters most: do not continue ascending — especially to a higher sleeping altitude — if symptoms persist. Most of the "moderate/difficult" grading you'll see across this document already builds in acclimatization days for exactly this reason — don't skip them to save time.

When it gets serious: confusion, staggering, or loss of coordination signals HACE (high altitude cerebral edema); breathlessness at rest, persistent

cough, or frothy sputum signals HAPE (high altitude pulmonary edema) — both are life- threatening and can progress to death within about 12 hours. The only real treatment is immediate descent, with medication and oxygen if available.

Diamox (acetazolamide): the standard preventive medication, typically started 1-2 days before a high-altitude ascent — this is a prescription drug, so this isn't medical advice, just a flag that it exists and is widely used by trekkers on exactly this kind of terrain; talk to a doctor before your K2/GGLA or Snow Lake-tier trips specifically, given how high and sustained those are.", "metadata": {"page_start": 1, "source": "pakistan-north-tours-final.pdf", "page_end": 3}}, {"id": "p040-042-e594be504c6e", "text": "K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La (GGLA)

Corridor

Getting there

on the KKH) → cross the Indus bridge at Pattan → jeep track into Palas Valley. Kolai-Palas is its own district now, split from the rest of Kohistan, divided into accessible Lower Palas and the harder-to- reach Upper Palas.

Start point: Hopar/Nagar Valley (via Hoper, roughly 1 hour from Karimabad) — bike-accessible to Hopar.

What it is: Rush Lake sits over 4,700m — Pakistan's highest lake, reached by crossing the Bualtar and Barpu glaciers.

Getting there from Islamabad/Rawalpindi

By air: PIA, Airblue, and AirSial all fly Islamabad → Skardu (KDU) direct, about 1–1h10m in the air, roughly 24 weekly departures between them. Fares run roughly PKR 12,000–45,000 one-way depending on timing and season — book early, this route sells out fast in peak season (Eid, summer holidays). Flights are almost always morning departures since mountain visibility is best early, and weather cancellations are common — don't book it on a tight schedule.

By bike: The road distance is roughly 630–700 km, taking 12–14 hours of actual driving depending on route and conditions — realistically 2 days on a 125cc. Route: Islamabad → Hazara Motorway → Mansehra → Besham → Dasu → Chilas → Jaglot → turn off the

KKH onto the Skardu Road (S-1) → Skardu. The Skardu Road was rebuilt by FWO and is now mostly paved and smooth — noticeably better surface than parts of the KKH itself. Same fuel-stop logic as the Hunza run: fill up at every town, nothing reliable on the Jaglot–Skardu stretch.

By local bus: NATCO runs Islamabad/Rawalpindi → Skardu directly, fares around PKR 4,630–5,500 depending on bus class, with buses departing daily around 2pm and the trip taking the same 12–14 hours as the drive.

Skardu city — getting settled

Hotels: Range widely — popular mid-range options run roughly PKR 14,000–30,800/night, with luxury lakeside resorts near Kachura going up to PKR 67,750+. Budget guesthouses exist in Skardu city center at lower rates than this, though exact figures are harder to pin down online — worth checking on arrival or via Bookme.

What's in the city itself: Kharpocho Fort ("King of Forts," built late 17th century by Ali Sher Khan Anchan) overlooks the city and the confluence of the Indus and Shigar rivers, the Katpana Cold Desert (also called Biama Nakpo), Upper and Lower Kachura Lakes (Lower Kachura = Shangrila, with its famous red-roof resort), and Satpara Lake

(a dammed lake, built by Ali Sher Khan Anchan in the 1580s–1624).

Food: Balti cuisine leans on wheat, buckwheat, dried apricots and yak/beef rather than rice. Worth trying: Prapu (hand-made wheat noodles in a ground-walnut-and-apricot-oil sauce), Balay (a family of soups — Traspi Balay is the most notable), Mamtu (steamed dumplings, same as Hunza), and fresh trout — several fish farms around Kharmang and Khaplu serve it straight from the stream.", "metadata": {"source": "pakistan-north-tours-final.pdf", "page_start": 37, "page_end": 39}}, {"id": "p042-044-232729beb314", "text": "Khaplu Valley (Ghanche District)
